text:
maria: Quick experiment notes — ran a speculative-decode patch on ozma-mini-13b-q4 (draft quant). Observed ~1.9x token throughput and ~1.6x p50 latency improvement in our microbench, but a tiny ROUGE-L drop (~1.8 points) on the summarization holdout. attaching rough numbers.
kevin: nice. which speculative strategy? beam or sampling fallback?
maria: two-stage candidate approach: greedy fast-path with a 2-candidate speculative verifier, early-abort prob=0.12. kv_prefetch enabled. quant: q4_hybrid, int8 attention.
anya: can you paste the eval command you used? I want to re-run locally.
maria: sure:
```
./eval_harness \
  --model ozma-mini-13b-q4 \
  --speculative=2 \
  --early_abort=0.12 \
  --kv_prefetch=true \
  --tasks summarization,qa \
  --seed 42 \
  --batch 8
```
zach: what metric suite on summarization? ROUGE-L only or also human-approx (bertscore)?
maria: ROUGE-1/2/L + BERTScore-F1. ROUGE-L drop was most visible, BERTScore down ~0.8 pts. QA metrics (F1/EM) unchanged within noise.
kevin: any sign of hallucination increase in qualitative spot checks?
maria: did 50-case manual pass — marginally more shortcuts (truncated context occasionally). hypothesis: speculative predictor sometimes returns shorter continuations causing verifier to backtrack less often => slight context drift.
anya: interesting. could be sequence-length bias in greedy predictor after quantization. did you try warming KV cache longer?
maria: yes, warmup didn't change the delta much. But disabling `kv_prefetch` reduced speedup and also reduced ROUGE drop (closer to baseline). Tradeoff looks real.
ci-bot: benchmark job 7311113001 completed — logs: https://ci/internal/arty/7311113001 — artifacts: /artifacts/7311113001/metrics.json
zach: can you push the exact harness and the holdout set id? I'll run the same with beamlet fallback (speculative_beam=4) and with no-quant fp16 to see baseline.
maria: holdout id `summ-holdout-v3` — uploaded to /datasets/holdouts/summ-holdout-v3. I'll add a branch with speculative_beam=4 and run fp16 baseline next.
kevin: let's also run a paired bootstrap to check significance on ROUGE-L. If it's < p=0.05 then we should treat as real regression.
anya: agreed. log the experiments in experiments/ozma-mini-q4/spec-grok-2026-03-21 and tag with `spec-grok`.
maria: noted. next steps: (1) run beamlet fallback + fp16 baseline, (2) paired bootstrap on ROUGE/BERTScore, (3) qualitative triage on the 20 most regressed queries. tagging @zach for the qualitative.
zach: on it. will start reruns tonight and post a short summary.
maria: thanks — will follow up tomorrow with consolidated metrics and the branch link. :rocket:
